_comment: Routes that exist ONLY in the desktop build. This is NOT a Go golden, and
it is the one file in this directory that is not.
read_routes.json and write_routes.json were generated by a chi.Walk over
the router server.New built, and #391 froze them when the Go tree was
deleted. Neither can record a route Go never had without ceasing to be
what it is -- a record of Go's surface. Leaving the desktop-only routes in
no file at all was the alternative, and it was rejected: those files exist
so the route surface cannot drift silently, and a whole family recorded
nowhere would weaken exactly that property.
So this file is the third table, with the same row shape and one stronger
guarantee. The two Go files are asserted in ONE direction -- the Rust test
iterates their rows, so a route that is claimed and never recorded passes.
Here the module under test exposes its routes as a single const (see
native::security::ROUTES) and the assertion is set equality, so a route
cannot be added, removed or renamed without this file moving.
'status' is 'native' or 'dropped', as in read_routes.json. Nothing is
'deferred': there is no second implementation left to defer to.
Nothing regenerates this file. It is authored alongside the code, and the
test is what keeps the two honest.

routes.reason: the public key, its kid and where both files live; write-scoped, because it names the private key's path
replaces the install's keypair, which refuses every token ever issued including the caller's own
the issued tokens, revoked ones included; write-scoped, because it enumerates every credential on the machine
mints a scoped token and returns the only copy of it that will ever exist
revokes one token by jti; an UPDATE rather than a DELETE, because removing the row would un-revoke it
the public key in JWKS form, UNAUTHENTICATED by design -- it is what a credential is verified against, so requiring one would be a bootstrap problem with no answer
